mathematics.independent_solution: After a common quarter-turn J, corresponding second directions are independently +/-Ju and +/-Jv. Both signs same gives y=x; mixed signs gives y=180-x. Acute/acute and obtuse/obtuse each exclude the latter.

option_checks.derivation: The claim that one direction must be same and one opposite is false: first 0/30 and second 90/120 are both same after a positive quarter-turn and both acute 30. Moreover the claimed 180-x alternative has the opposite type from x and cannot cover either same-type hypothesis.

A specified positive quarter-turn of first directions 0/30 gives 90/120, whereas permissible second directions 270/300 are both opposite and still acute 30. Obtuse analog: first 0/120, images 90/210, second 270/30, both obtuse 120. Thus the unconditional both-same claim and refusal to consider opposite rays are invalid, even though y=x is the true theorem. An unstated adaptive turn/alignment proof is not added.

Translation preserves side direction, so it cannot make the first side coincide with its perpendicular corresponding ray. The initial alignment step is impossible for a defined ray and cannot be repaired by the later quarter-turn.

The three stated relation types exhaust the four +/- choices: ++ and -- preserve x, +- and -+ yield 180-x. For x<90 the supplement is obtuse; for x>90 it is acute. Both same-type branches therefore force y=x.
